title: A buffered read is not held to the request's memory ceiling, so one `select` can take the whole host.
text: `nvs_runtime::Ctx::over_memory_limit` is polled between two Novis statements and once ahead of every `Core` member, and `queried_rows` materializes an entire result set inside one such call: `sqlite_rows`' `while let Some(row)` appends until the server stops sending, and the three wire arms do the same. Measured on this tree, a `select` of a hundred thousand rows a hundred thousand characters wide held ten gigabytes under a `[limits] memory` of 256M with no `FATAL`, while the same bytes accumulated from Novis stop at the ceiling. That breaks `rule:programs/memory-priority`'s bound that memory stays attributable and under an enforceable cap, which is priority 1 rather than a footprint question. The fix is a poll inside the row loop, and it is a decision about the seam rather than about one member: none of the four `*_rows` arms is handed a `Ctx` at all — they take a `QueryWatch` — so charging the ceiling means threading the request through them and through `schema`'s catalog reads, and deciding whether the poll is per row or per batch of them. `stream` is the member that already has the bound, because its walk returns to a statement boundary between rows. `tests/hostile/core/Db-Connection/query/01-values-that-do-not-match-and-more-rows-than-fit.nvs` step 6 is the attack, and it is marked `known-gap` for this entry.
